g.text: A single connection handles one request at a time. If you fire 5 calls, request #2 has to wait for request #1's
response before it can go. This called head-of-line blocking. To work around it, client need to open separated
connections, which cost more with new handshake handling.
Many requests and responses share one connection at the same time interleaved, no waiting in line.
One handshake, one connection, all the call flowiing concurrently

raw binary framing. The browser's fetch/XHR
